c1-bioetika-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Germline Editing Is Different
c1-bioetika-01.scenario: A discussion group on medical ethics is talking about gene editing.
c1-bioetika-01.prompt: Say why changing the germline is more controversial than treating one patient.
cues: Say that the change is heritable
c1-bioetika-01.target: A csíravonal-módosítás örökíthető, ezért az utódokat is érinti.
c1-bioetika-01.english: Germline modification is heritable, so it also affects the descendants.
c1-bioetika-01.canDo: I can explain why changing the germline is more controversial than treating one patient.

c1-bioetika-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Presumed Consent
c1-bioetika-02.scenario: A discussion group on medical ethics is talking about organ donation.
c1-bioetika-02.prompt: Explain what presumed consent means in Hungary.
cues: Say who counts as a donor
c1-bioetika-02.target: A feltételezett beleegyezés azt jelenti, hogy az elhunyt donor, hacsak életében nem tiltakozott.
c1-bioetika-02.english: Presumed consent means that the deceased is a donor unless they objected in life.
c1-bioetika-02.canDo: I can explain what presumed consent means in organ donation (*feltételezett beleegyezés*).

c1-bioetika-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Views of the Embryo
c1-bioetika-03.scenario: A discussion group on medical ethics is talking about stem cell research.
c1-bioetika-03.prompt: Set out the two views on the moral status of the embryo.
cues: Give the view that dignity starts at conception
c1-bioetika-03.target: Az egyik nézet szerint a méltóság a fogantatással kezdődik, a másik szerint a morális státusz fokozatosan fejlődik ki.
c1-bioetika-03.english: According to one view dignity begins at conception, according to the other the moral status develops gradually.
c1-bioetika-03.canDo: I can set out two views on the moral status of the embryo (*embrió erkölcsi státusza*).

c1-bioetika-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Karsai Case
c1-bioetika-04.scenario: A discussion group on medical ethics is talking about the Karsai case.
c1-bioetika-04.prompt: Say who Dániel Karsai was and what he asked the court in Strasbourg.
cues: Say which right he relied on
c1-bioetika-04.target: Karsai Dániel alkotmányjogász volt, és a strasbourgi bíróságon a magánélet tiszteletben tartásához való jogra hivatkozott.
c1-bioetika-04.english: Dániel Karsai was a constitutional lawyer, and at the Strasbourg court he relied on the right to respect for private life.
c1-bioetika-04.canDo: I can describe the Karsai case and the question it raised about dying with dignity.

c1-bioetika-05.title: Communicative Challenge: AI in Diagnosis
c1-bioetika-05.scenario: A discussion group on medical ethics is talking about AI in hospitals.
c1-bioetika-05.prompt: Say what AI changes in diagnosis and what the doctor still does.
cues: Say what the algorithm does quickly
Say what the doctor still does
c1-bioetika-05.target: Az algoritmus gyorsan áttekinti a felvételeket, de a beteggel az orvos beszél, empátiával.
c1-bioetika-05.english: The algorithm looks through the images quickly, but the doctor talks to the patient, with empathy.
c1-bioetika-05.canDo: I can discuss what AI changes in diagnosis and what the doctor still does.

c1-bioetika-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Dilemmas of the Unit
c1-bioetika-consolidation.scenario: A discussion group on medical ethics sums up the unit.
c1-bioetika-consolidation.prompt: Name one dilemma from this unit and say why it is hard.
c1-bioetika-consolidation.target: A fagyasztott embriók sorsa nehéz kérdés, mert a vágyott gyermek és az embrió méltósága ütközik.
c1-bioetika-consolidation.english: The fate of frozen embryos is a hard question, because the wished-for child and the dignity of the embryo clash.
c1-bioetika-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the main dilemmas of this unit: gene editing, organ donation, the embryo, dying with dignity and AI in medicine.
